basics.name: Wenwei Cai (蔡文炜)
basics.summary: PhD student in the Department of Chemistry at HKUST, working with Prof. Lixue Cheng on AI for energy materials. My research combines first-principles calculations, molecular dynamics, literature mining, and LLM-based multi-agent systems for electrolyte design and materials discovery.
basics.label: PhD Student in Chemistry (Scientific Computation)

work.position: Multi-Agent Electrolyte Design via Literature-Grounded Reasoning and Iterative Optimization
work.summary: Developed an LLM-based platform for lithium battery electrolyte formulation design.
highlights: Coordinated expert agents with LangGraph to propose, critique, and refine formulations under user-defined constraints.
Implemented hierarchical retrieval-augmented generation with FAISS, source tracking, and agent-specific literature access.
Designed an ionic-liquid bridge agent to translate coordination chemistry and ion-transport evidence into formulation guidance.
Built persistent task memory and a React–FastAPI application for interactive design and literature questions.

work.position: AI-Driven Discovery of High-Performance Solid-State Electrolytes
work.summary: Built a literature-based knowledge base and began developing a generative design framework for solid-state electrolytes.
highlights: Fine-tuned DeBERTa v3 to classify approximately 115,000 papers and identify 17,000 relevant articles.
Used Gemini 2.5 Pro to extract 97,000 material-property records and standardize formulas and units.
Developing multi-objective optimization with generative and surrogate models.

work.position: Polarized Ni⁰-Niδ⁺ Catalysts for CO₂ Electroreduction
work.summary: Used full-solvent AIMD and the slow-growth approach to investigate C–C coupling at partially polarized nickel and extend mechanistic insights to other metals.

work.position: Confined Proton Transport in Layered Manganese Oxide Electrodes
work.summary: Used AIMD to investigate how interlayer spacing, proton concentration, and hydrogen-bond environments affect proton transport in δ-MnO₂.
Led a national undergraduate innovation project on bismuth-based catalysts, including synthesis, electrochemical testing, characterization, and reconstruction analysis.
